title: Canonical Transition Maps Between Generalized Lattice Models
body_html:
Canonical Transition Maps Between Generalized Lattice Models

This node defines the transition maps $T_{x,y}$ between the generalized lattice models attached to points $x,y\in\mathcal B(\operatorname{Sp}(W))$ without choosing any auxiliary Lagrangian or self-dual lattice $A$, and records their composition law. The earlier $A$-test-vector construction is recovered as one trivialization of the composition cocycle, not as part of the model. The parahoric action is not used here; only the $H(W)$-structure.

Throughout, $H(W)=W\times F$ is the Heisenberg group with $(u,t)(u',t')=(u+u',\,t+t'+\tfrac12\langle u,u'\rangle)$, and $\psi$ is the fixed additive character (conductor $\mathfrak p$). The coefficient ring $R$ is any field with $\operatorname{char}R\neq p$; no Hermitian/unitary structure is assumed.

The model is $A$-free

By Generalized Lattice Model, for each $x$ the finite symplectic space $\mathsf b_x=\mathscr L_{x,0}/\mathscr L_{x,0+}$ over the residue field carries a finite Heisenberg group $H(\mathsf b_x)$ with a unique irreducible representation $(\overline\omega_x,\mathbf S(\mathsf b_x))$ of central character $\overline\psi$ (finite Stone–von Neumann). The generalized lattice model

$$ \Omega_x=\mathcal S(\mathscr L_{x,0}) =\Big\{\,f:W\to\mathbf S(\mathsf b_x)\ \text{loc.\ const.,\ cpt.\ supp.\ mod }\mathscr L_{x,0}\ :\ f(a+w)=\psi\!\big(\tfrac12\langle w,a\rangle\big)\,\overline\omega_x(\bar a)\,f(w),\ a\in\mathscr L_{x,0}\Big\} $$

uses only the abstract representation $\mathbf S(\mathsf b_x)$ and its abstract action $\overline\omega_x$, both of which are determined by $\mathsf b_x$ alone. A Lagrangian $A\subseteq\mathsf b_x$ is needed only if one insists on a Schrödinger realization $\mathbf S(\mathsf b_x)\cong R[\mathsf b_x/A]$; it is not part of the data of $\Omega_x$. Thus $\Omega_x$ depends on $x$ alone. Each $\Omega_x$ is a model of the unique irreducible smooth representation $(\omega_\psi,\mathcal H)$ of $H(W)$ with central character $\psi$ (Loke–Ma, Section 2.3); by Stone–von Neumann all $\Omega_x$ are isomorphic $H(W)$-representations and $\dim_R\operatorname{Hom}_{H(W)}(\Omega_x,\Omega_y)=1$.

The canonical distinguished subspace $S_x$

For each $x$, the lattice $\mathscr L_{x,0+}=\mathscr L_{x,0}^{*}$ is isotropic mod conductor, so it embeds in $H(W)$ via $\ell\mapsto(\ell,0)$ and the lattice-fixed subspace is defined:

$$ S_x:=\Omega_x^{\,\mathscr L_{x,0+}}=\{\,v\in\Omega_x:\omega_\psi(\ell,0)\,v=v\ \ \forall\,\ell\in\mathscr L_{x,0+}\,\}. $$

This is exactly $S_L$ of Lattice Fixed Vector Model with $L=\mathscr L_{x,0+}$, which the source records as independent of the auxiliary lattice $A$ and of the intertwining map between realizations. It is finite-dimensional, with $\dim_R S_x=\dim_R\mathbf S(\mathsf b_x)=|\mathsf b_x|^{1/2}$, and depends on $x$ alone.

  • At a generic point $x_0$ (interior of an alcove) all $a_i\in(0,\tfrac12)$ are off the walls $a_i\in\tfrac12\mathbb Z$, so $0$ is not a jump of $\mathscr L_{x_0}$ and $\mathscr L_{x_0,0}=\mathscr L_{x_0,0+}$ is self-dual; then $\mathsf b_{x_0}=0$, $\dim_R S_{x_0}=1$, and $S_{x_0}=R\cdot\mathbf 1_{\mathscr L_{x_0,0}}$ is the canonical vacuum line, with canonical generator the characteristic function $\mathbf 1_{\mathscr L_{x_0,0}}$ (no $A$).

Definition of the transition maps

For each ordered pair $(x,y)$ there is, up to a scalar, a unique $H(W)$-intertwiner $\Omega_x\to\Omega_y$ (Stone–von Neumann). Fix one generic reference point $x_0$ as above with canonical vacuum $v_0=\mathbf 1_{\mathscr L_{x_0,0}}$, and normalize the scalar by the distinguished data $S_\bullet$:

$$ \boxed{\;T_{x,y}\colon\Omega_x\to\Omega_y\ \text{ is the unique }H(W)\text{-intertwiner whose restriction } S_x\to S_y\text{ is the canonical lattice-fixed transition }\tau_{x,y}.\;} $$

Here $\tau_{x,y}\colon S_x\to S_y$ is the canonical averaging map inside the common model: writing $e_y$ for the normalized averaging idempotent over $\mathscr L_{y,0+}$,

$$ e_y=\frac{1}{[\mathscr L_{y,0+}:\mathscr L^{0}]}\sum_{\ell\in\mathscr L_{y,0+}/\mathscr L^{0}}\omega_\psi(\ell,0) \ :\ \Omega_y\to S_y,\qquad \tau_{x,y}:=e_y\circ(\text{inclusion of }S_x), $$

with $\mathscr L^{0}$ any open subgroup of $\mathscr L_{x,0+}\cap\mathscr L_{y,0+}$ acting trivially on the relevant level (the value is independent of the choice). The only denominator is $[\mathscr L_{y,0+}:\mathscr L^{0}]$, a power of $q$, hence invertible in $R$ since $\operatorname{char}R\neq p$. Each ingredient — $\Omega_x$, $S_x$, $e_y$, $v_0$ — is $A$-free, so $T_{x,y}$ is $A$-free.

At the generic reference, $S_{x_0}=R\,v_0$ is a line, so $T_{x,x_0}$ is pinned by a single canonical scalar ($\tau_{x,x_0}(v)$ is a multiple of $v_0$); this is the clean normalization the construction is anchored on. The explicit integral kernel of $T_{x,y}$ on the function realizations is the lattice-model transition operator of Loke–Ma, Section 2.3; it is not needed below.

Composition law

For all $x,y,z$ the maps are $H(W)$- and $\operatorname{Mp}(W)$-equivariant isomorphisms, and

$$ T_{x,x}=\mathrm{id}_{\Omega_x},\qquad T_{y,z}\circ T_{x,y}=\delta_{x,y,z}\cdot T_{x,z}, \qquad \delta_{x,y,z}\in R^{\times}. $$

The scalar $\delta_{x,y,z}$ is a finite Gauss-sum / Weil index — the $2$-cocycle of the metaplectic cover $\operatorname{Mp}(W)\to\operatorname{Sp}(W)$ evaluated on the lattice data — and is a root of unity in $R$. Because every $T_{x,y}$ is $A$-free, $\delta_{x,y,z}$ is intrinsic: it is not an artifact of any choice of $A$, and it is the gauge-invariant content of the splitting character $\delta^{\mathrm{lm}}$ recorded in lattice_model_transition.self_dual_test_vector_normalization.

What is proved vs.\ open. That each $T_{x,y}$ is a well-defined $A$-free $H(W)$-intertwiner, and that the composition law holds with some scalar $\delta_{x,y,z}\in R^\times$, follows from Stone–von Neumann and the cyclicity of $v_0$ exactly as in the test-vector argument (a nonzero $H(W)$-intertwiner of irreducibles is unique up to scalar; composites are again such intertwiners). The identification of $\delta_{x,y,z}$ with the explicit Weil index requires the metaplectic-cocycle computation of Loke–Ma, Section 2.3 (gap: not reproduced here).

$A$ as a trivialization, and the compatible-system question

The exact cocycle $T_{y,z}\circ T_{x,y}=T_{x,z}$ holds iff $\delta_{x,y,z}=1$, i.e.\ iff $\delta$ is trivialized.

A common self-dual lattice $A$ for a family $\mathcal X$ provides exactly such a trivialization: if all points of $\mathcal X$ lie in the closure of one facet then Level-0 Lattice Under Specialization to a Face gives a smallest level-$0$ lattice $\mathscr L_{\ast,0}$ with $\mathscr L_{\ast,0}\subseteq\mathscr L_{x,0}$ for every $x$; a Lagrangian of $\mathsf b_\ast=\mathscr L_{\ast,0}/\mathscr L_{\ast,0+}$ (residue field of odd order) lifts to a common self-dual $A=A^{\#}$ with $A\subseteq\mathscr L_{x,0}$ for all $x$. Renormalizing each $T_{x,y}$ by the common $A$-test line replaces $\delta_{x,y,z}$ by a coboundary, hence by $1$ over $\mathcal X$. So the old $A$-construction does not remove the content of $\delta$; it chooses a (non-canonical) trivialization of it over an incident set. Equivalently, the metaplectic cover splits over the common parahoric data, the splitting being parametrized by the choice of $A$.

The compatible-system problem is therefore: does $\delta$ admit a canonical ($A$-free) trivialization over the whole building (or over the relevant incident poset)? This is the gauge-coboundary question for $\delta^{\mathrm{lm}}$ and is not settled here.
